title: Show HN: GPT Plays Civilization
text: Hey HN, I've always been a big fan of the Civ games, and was always frustrated at how terrible the AI was. So I got curious about whether LLMs could play Civ well, or not! I thought about having the agents interact with the GUI directly, but something about that seemed like the wrong approach. For one thing, it seemed to me like images would cost way more in tokens. For another, LLMs seem like a different kind of intelligence from humans, so why would an interface meant for humans be optimal for them? Anyway, I spend a few weeks modifying Unciv [0], an open-source reimplementation of Civ V to have the right endpoints and views for an agent to be able to play civ in the same way a person could. You can see the first game running at the link. So far, it looks like the GPT models are able to play a reasonable game - definitely better than the built-in AI, which was my barometer for success! title: Show HN: Pasteup – Paste screenshots into file upload fields
text: I'm currently a CS student, so that means a lot of file uploads to my university's janky website. I hated having to sort through the file picker just to attach an assignment open the next tab over. Pasteup is a Chrome extension that lets you press Cmd+V / Ctrl+V on the page instead, it finds the corresponding file box and attaches them automatically (if there are multiple it opens a picker). Moreover I added an automatic file converter, so for things like CSV, txt, and code, it automatically converts it to the right format. This means my workflow went from going to the assignment sorting through 15 finder folders and uploading to ctrl a ctrl c ctrl v. The file converter is pretty smart, and supports a lot of formats. If the field only takes PDF or JPG, it converts the file before uploading. It also turns copied spreadsheet cells into a CSV, JSON into a .json, and Figma's "Copy as SVG" into an image. If you're already in any text boxes or editors it does nothing. If the site handles paste itself (FilePond, chat apps), it goes first, and Pasteup does nothing. It runs entirely locally: no servers, no analytics, no network requests, no third-party libraries. I'd love to hear about sites where it picks the wrong field or gets in the way or just any feedback in general!

title: Show HN: bouncemarket – a live prediction market game for a bouncing ball
text: a ball will fall. trade on where it lands. I made this game! Some technical details: The entire drop of the ball is simulated server-side, then streamed to each client as server-sent events with a small buffer. Every drop is deterministic from its starting position, so rounds can be replayed exactly for later analysis, but tiny variations in starting position can change the ultimate outcome. There's some AI traders to keep the market moving, but they drop out in any round that has more than five people. They operate using a naive set of rules that I wrote for them, so they're not too hard to beat -- it's when the market is full of real people that it gets tricky. Curious to get feedback on anything you would change, and especially whether the mechanics were clear right away or not.

title: Show HN: DragDropMath – Learn math by feel
text: Hi HN! I am a professional physicist and I shuffle symbols in equations and mathematical expressions all day long. During my PhD (almost 20 years ago) I noticed that it is as if the symbols have their own 'physics', which makes the wrong moves impossible and the right ones obvious. So I created DragDropMath, where you can learn how to simplify mathematical expressions and how to solve equations by dragging symbols around, and only correct moves are allowed, so you get to feel what's right without experiencing (and so learning) wrong moves. I always wanted to make this, but life got in the way. Then a few weeks ago I saw declarative dragging ( https://declarative-dragging.github.io/ ) on the front page of HN and the spark came back! It took quite a few rounds to get the feel right, but I think it's close to what happens in my mind when I mentally manipulate these expressions. A few more points: - There are no ads, no trackers, no accounts (it's a static website and progress is saved in the browser cache). - Teachers can create their own problem sets, encoded in the link. - I plan to add more chapters (trigonometry, complex numbers, some calculus) but I first need to figure out the 'right' mode of interaction. - I just started working on the experience from mobile, so there may still be some rough edges there I'm curious to know what you think, if you have suggestions for content, if you spot anything that I should fix, if you have feature requests! title: Thirty First Meeting of the Standing Advisory Committee (SAC) to Review the Flow of Credit to the MSME Sector in Kolkata on November 27, 2026
text: The 31st meeting of the Standing Advisory Committee (SAC) to review the flow of credit to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) was held in Kolkata on November 27, 2026. Shri Swaminathan J, Deputy Governor, Reserve Bank of India (RBI), chaired the meeting. Participants included the Additional Secretary and Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME, and the Joint Secretary, Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance. Managing directors and executive directors of select banks, heads of SIDBI, NABARD, CGTMSE, NCGTC and KVIC, the Chief Executive Officer of the Indian Banks’ Association, and representatives of national, regional and state-level MSME associations also attended. Recognising MSMEs’ contribution to India’s economy and development goals, the Deputy Governor urged banks to expedite credit sanctions and reduce reliance on collateral through cash-flow-based lending using ULI and other digital channels. He called for greater use of TReDS for receivables financing and early identification and resolution of stress. He invited industry associations to actively participate in outreach events such as RBI’s town halls and district-level MSME SAMVAAD meetings to improve awareness and raise their members’ concerns with banks. The Committee reviewed working capital and investment credit to MSMEs, lending to first-time borrowers and credit guarantee coverage. It also discussed the higher limit for collateral-free lending to micro and small enterprises, settlement of CPSE invoices through TReDS and key provisions of the MSMED (Amendment) Act, 2026. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1581

text: RBI/2026-27/310 DoR.RET.REC.262/12.01.001/2026-27 November 27, 2026 All Scheduled Banks, Madam / Sir, Section 42(1) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 - Change in Daily Minimum Cash Reserve Maintenance Requirement Please refer to our circular DoR.RET.REC.247/12.01.001/2026-27 dated October 09, 2026 on the captioned subject. 2.
